evidence: Remote experiment outputs/acwm-open-models/20260810T154728Z-e2d30e20 contains three 81-frame same-case, same-seed native OSCAR candidates and per-candidate evaluation evidence.
Candidates 000 and 001 articulate the robot but leave the yellow bowl static, producing zero action adherence.
Candidate 002 moves the bowl somewhat upward and rightward but misses the declared terminal-progress gate.

The batch exposed a duplicate-case adapter bug: dictionary pairing collapsed repeated slide-right requests and caused the workflow evaluator to revisit one evidence directory. The adapter now pairs backend results in strict request order and regression tests cover duplicate case IDs.
lessons: Prompt-only repair cannot substitute for a trajectory whose contact and vertical phases are already demonstrated by the model.
Same-case candidate batches require order-preserving result pairing; case_id is not a unique request key.
limitations: None of the three candidates passed the complete automatic and human acceptance protocol.
next_actions: Compile a lift-then-carry trajectory from the successful lift-up vertical template and resample one native OSCAR candidate.
scope: Three same-seed native OSCAR prompt-repair candidates for direct slide-right
summary: Three articulated prompt variants generated successfully, but none established the required causal rightward bowl motion; the batch also revealed and led to a fix for duplicate-case result pairing.
